input_messages.content: Hi there! I’m having trouble sending MMS messages from my phone. It’s been happening for the past few hours, and I’d really like to get it working again. Can you help me figure out what’s going on?
Sure! My name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know what you need me to do next.
I checked, and my messaging app currently cannot send MMS messages. What should I try next?
Looking at my phone’s status bar, I see that Airplane Mode is currently on. I don’t see any signal bars or mobile data icons. What should I do next?
I’ve turned off Airplane Mode, but now my status bar shows “No Signal” and “Data Disabled.” I still can’t send MMS messages. What should I try next?
I checked the SIM status, and it says that no SIM card is detected in the phone. What should I do next?
I reseated the SIM card, and now my status bar shows a poor signal, 2G, and that data is enabled. What should I do next?
I changed the network mode to “4G/5G preferred,” and now my status bar shows an excellent signal with 5G and data enabled. What should I do next?
I tried sending an MMS message again, but it still isn’t working. My messaging app still can’t send MMS messages. What should I try next?
I checked my APN settings, and it looks like the MMSC URL for picture messages is not set. Could this be causing the problem? What should I do next?
I reset the APN settings to default and rebooted my phone, but I still can’t send MMS messages. The messaging app still says it can’t send MMS. Is there anything else I should try?
I turned off Wi-Fi Calling and tried sending an MMS again, but it still isn’t working. The app still can’t send MMS messages. What else can I try?
I checked my messaging app’s permissions, and it already has permission for SMS and phone, but not for storage. Should I go ahead and grant storage permission to the messaging app?
I granted storage permission to the messaging app and tried sending an MMS again, but it still isn’t working. The app still can’t send MMS messages. Is there anything else I should try?

Thank you for providing your information, John. To help you with your MMS issue, I’ll need you to perform a few quick checks on your phone. 

First, could you please check if you can send MMS messages using your messaging app? If your phone has a diagnostic tool or option to "check if you can send MMS," please use it and let me know the result.

If you’re not sure how to do this, let me know, and I’ll guide you through the steps!
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I checked, and my messaging app currently cannot send MMS messages. What should I try next?

Thank you for checking. Since your messaging app cannot send MMS messages, let’s go through some troubleshooting steps. First, we need to make sure your phone has cellular service and mobile data enabled, as both are required for MMS.

Could you please check your phone’s status bar and let me know:
- If you see any signal bars (indicating cellular service)
- If mobile data is enabled (look for 4G, 5G, LTE, or similar icons)
- If Airplane Mode is on (an airplane icon)

Let me know what you see, or if you need instructions on how to check this.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
Looking at my phone’s status bar, I see that Airplane Mode is currently on. I don’t see any signal bars or mobile data icons. What should I do next?

Airplane Mode disables all wireless connections, including cellular service and mobile data, which are required for sending MMS messages. 

Please turn off Airplane Mode on your phone. After you do this, check if your signal bars and mobile data icons reappear in the status bar. Once Airplane Mode is off and you see signal bars, try sending an MMS message again.

Let me know if this resolves the issue or if you need further assistance!

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
I’ve turned off Airplane Mode, but now my status bar shows “No Signal” and “Data Disabled.” I still can’t send MMS messages. What should I try next?

Thank you for the update. Since your phone now shows “No Signal” and “Data Disabled,” let’s address these issues step by step:

1. First, let’s check if your SIM card is properly recognized by your phone. Please check your SIM card status (there may be a diagnostic option called “check SIM status” on your device). Let me know if it says “Active,” “Missing,” or “Locked.”

2. After that, we’ll work on enabling mobile data.

Please let me know the result of the SIM status check. If you need instructions on how to check this, let me know!
No SIM card detected in the phone.
I checked the SIM status, and it says that no SIM card is detected in the phone. What should I do next?

Since your phone is not detecting the SIM card, please try reseating the SIM card. This means removing the SIM card from your phone and then reinserting it to ensure it is properly seated.

Most phones have a diagnostic or troubleshooting option called “reseat SIM card.” Please use this option if available, or physically remove and reinsert the SIM card if you are comfortable doing so.

After reseating the SIM card, check your status bar again to see if the signal bars and mobile data icons appear. Let me know what you see, or if you need further instructions!

SIM card re-seated successfully.

I reseated the SIM card, and now my status bar shows a poor signal, 2G, and that data is enabled. What should I do next?

Great progress! Now that your phone detects the SIM card and data is enabled, but you’re only seeing a 2G connection with poor signal, this could affect your ability to send MMS messages. MMS typically requires at least a 3G connection.

Let’s try improving your network connection:
Please check your phone’s network mode preference. If it’s set to 2G or 3G only, change it to “4G/5G preferred” or “4G only” if available. This will allow your phone to connect to faster networks if they are available in your area.

After changing the network mode, wait a moment and see if your phone connects to a stronger signal (3G, 4G, or 5G). Let me know what network type and signal strength you see in your status bar after making this change.

Let me know if the MMS sends successfully or if you still encounter any issues. If it doesn’t work, we’ll continue with the next troubleshooting steps.

Thank you for letting me know. Since you have good signal and data, the next step is to check your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings, as incorrect APN settings can prevent MMS from working.

Please check your APN settings on your phone. If there’s a diagnostic option called “check APN settings,” use it and let me know if it shows any errors or if the MMSC URL is missing or incorrect.

If you need instructions on how to check your APN settings, let me know!

Yes, a missing MMSC URL in your APN settings will prevent MMS messages from being sent or received. To fix this, please reset your APN settings to the default values. Most phones have a “reset APN settings” option in the network or mobile data settings.

After resetting the APN settings, you must reboot your device for the changes to take effect.

Please:
1. Reset your APN settings to default.
2. Reboot your phone.

Once your phone restarts, try sending an MMS message again. Let me know if this resolves the issue or if you need further assistance!
